title: Cloud platform adoption
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's dive into our cloud migration strategy. I've been looking into various options and I'd like to present my findings.

SRE: Before we start, I just want to bring up the potential issues with vendor lock-in we might face.

CTO: I agree, SRE. Let's make sure we keep that in mind when discussing the options.

Finance Partner: That's a valid concern, but we can't ignore the financial implications either. So, let's hear what you've got, Platform Engineering Lead.

Platform Engineering Lead: As you know, we've been considering three main options: Google Cloud Platform, Microsoft Azure, and building our own on-premises data center.

SRE: I've looked into Google Cloud, and while it's a powerful platform, it doesn't seamlessly integrate with our existing data pipeline using Snowflake.

Platform Engineering Lead: I concur. The same issue arises with Azure as well. Their pricing model for elastic workloads is more expensive in the long run.

Finance Partner: Building an in-house solution would require a significant upfront investment and prolong our time-to-market. So, we're effectively left with one option – AWS.

SRE: (sighs) I understand the financial aspects, but AWS could still pose a problem due to potential vendor lock-in and increased maintenance burden.

CTO: Those are valid concerns, but AWS does offer a broad range of services that align well with our current tech stack and data pipeline.

Platform Engineering Lead: Plus, the estimated time-to-value with AWS is significantly shorter compared to a self-hosted solution.

SRE: I see your point, but we need to consider caveats and open risks as well.

Platform Engineering Lead: Absolutely. Pending a final assessment of AWS's data privacy and compliance with our acquirer's requirements. Also, assuming a successful implementation of custom integrations between AWS and Snowflake.

SRE: Those are important considerations. But I'd like to emphasize the vendor lock-in and maintenance burden once again.

CTO: I understand your concerns, SRE. We can mitigate vendor lock-in by using open-source tools and making sure we keep our solutions agnostic as much as possible. As for maintenance, it will be a shared responsibility between SRE and our platform engineering team.

Finance Partner: Agreed. We'll have to monitor the costs closely to avoid any unexpected increases.

Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, with those concerns addressed, I propose we adopt AWS cloud platform with custom integrations on a provisional basis.

SRE: On a provisional basis, I can agree to that. But let's keep a close eye on the potential issues we discussed.

CTO: Agreed. We'll take this decision provisionally for now, and continue to monitor and address any issues that arise.

Finance Partner: Understood. Let's move forward, and I'll start working on the financial modeling for our AWS migration.

(off-topic exchange)

SRE: By the way, have we heard anything back from the new coffee shop downtown? I heard they have great lattes.

Platform Engineering Lead: Actually, I passed by it the other day and it did look inviting. We should definitely check it out.

SRE: Absolutely! Maybe next week, after we've made some progress on the AWS migration.

(back to discussion)

CTO: Agreed. Let's focus on the AWS migration first, and then we can indulge in that coffee.

Platform Engineering Lead: Sounds good to me. Let's get started.

Title: Decision Record - Cloud Infrastructure Selection

Based on the discussion, a provisional decision has been made to adopt AWS Cloud Platform for its compatibility with our current tech stack and data pipeline. This choice assumes a successful implementation of custom integrations between AWS and Snowflake.

Google Cloud Platform does not offer seamless integration with our existing data pipeline using Snowflake. Building an in-house solution would require a substantial upfront investment and could potentially prolong our time-to-market.

The estimated time-to-value with AWS is significantly shorter compared to a self-hosted solution. However, a final assessment of AWS's data privacy and compliance with our acquirer's requirements is still pending. No further details regarding alternative options or concerns were included in this record.
